keyframe_review.note: 79,310 km2 for 404-367 (no infobox area). The Hebei plain is right only for the Zhongshan Wei held: 'in 407, Zhongshan was conquered by Wei troops, led by general Yue Yang' (Zhongshan page; the Marquess Wen page: 'eliminated in 406 BCE') until 'in 381, Zhongshan won its independence back'. The shape lacks Anyi, the capital, and Xihe, the land between the Yellow and Luo rivers that Wu Qi took in 409-406. Added; years 403-382. Revised 2026-10-19: the 403-382 plain is cut to the Zhongshan core (Lingshou in Pingshan County, Dongyuan in Zhengding County, the Great Wall at Baoding; Zhongshan page, re-read: 'in 407, Zhongshan was conquered by Wei troops'; 'in 381, Zhongshan won its independence back'). The rest of Cliopatria's 429 cells (Handan, Xingtai, Ye, Hengshui, Cangzhou) is dropped: the Zhongshan page has no Wei holding there, the Handan page does not say who held Handan between 588 and 386 ('In 386 BCE, Marquess Jing of Zhao officially relocated the capital to Handan') and the zhao dossier no longer claims Handan before 386 either, so those cells belong to nobody on the pages. Dingzhou, which the reviewer named, is on no Zhongshan page I opened and is not in the core.

Anyi with Hedong and Xihe remain. Revised: the Hebei and Shandong parts of Wei are page-silent and left out. The Wei page (re-read 2026-10-19) says only that the territory 'lay between the states of Qin and Qi and included parts of modern-day Henan, Hebei, Shanxi, and Shandong' and names no place for Hebei or Shandong; it does not mention Hedong, Henei, Ye or Nanyang. Henei (the land north of the Yellow River between Anyi and Daliang) is on none of the pages opened as Wei's, so no disc is drawn for it; the Warring States page only says 'with Han in the south, Wei in the middle, and Zhao in the north'.

ledger.note: 376: 'In 376 BC, the states of Han, Wei and Zhao deposed Duke Jing of Jin' and divided the last Jin territory (Warring States page, re-read 2026-10-19). The Spring and Autumn table lists the last Jin land 'to Han and Zhao' only, the Jin dossier dissolves Jin in 369 to Han (Houma) and the Partition of Jin page has the division in 349; Wei's share is on the Warring States page alone, its place is not on any page, and the disc is the han dossier's reading (confidence 2: the year is the page's, the region is mine). It lies inside the Anyi/Hedong disc that the keyframes already hold.

361: King Hui moves the capital from Anyi to Daliang (Kaifeng). 'In 361 BC, King Hui of Wei relocated the Wei capital from the city of An...'; the state is also called Liang from this capital (Wei page).

208: Wei is restored after the Qin collapse (Wei Jiu, then Wei Bao). The Wei Bao page gives Wei Jiu's rising only as 'around this time' after 209 and his death 'the following year'; Cliopatria's 208 shape (Henan, Hebei, Shandong) is the only location (page silent).

206: Wei Bao is made King of Western Wei. Eighteen Kingdoms (created 'in 206 BCE' by Xiang Yu): Western Wei, Wei Bao, 'southern Shanxi', capital Pingyang (Wei Bao page). Revised: the land was Qin's before the collapse and the Eighteen Kingdoms were 'created by military leader Xiang Yu in 206 BCE', so the allocator is the Qin dynasty's successor order (western-chu holds the allocator's role in the ea-02 dossiers); the counterpart is not 'nobody'.

205: Han Xin captures Wei Bao and Western Wei ends. 'In October-November 205 BCE, Wei Bao personally led an attack on Han Xin but lost the battle and was captured'; the Eighteen Kingdoms table: 'Lost to Liu Bang'; the Wei Bao page: Hedong Commandery absorbed the territory.

wars.name: Qin's conquest of Wei

zones.text: Daliang (Kaifeng) and its district, all that is left of Wei after Anyi

wars.outcome: Qin victory: Wang Ben flooded Daliang and King Jia surrendered; Qin made the Dang and Sishui commanderies.

wars.name: Han Xin's conquest of Western Wei
wars.outcome: Han victory: Wei Bao, who had gone back to Chu in 205, was defeated and captured in October-November 205.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is on any page; Wei's frontiers with Qin (the Yellow River and Hedong), Han, Zhao and Qi are approximate, and the corrected shapes are discs around the named places.

sources.title: Qin's wars of unification
sources.note: Qin conquests of Han (230), Zhao (236-222), Wei (225); the 364 and 307 defeats of Han.

sources.title: Warring States period
sources.note: Thin on territory: 376 division of the last Jin land, 340 and 318 Wei events, 230-225 conquests. Opened for Han, Wei, Zhao, Zheng. Re-read 2026-10-19: the 376 sentence and 'with Han in the south, Wei in the middle, and Zhao in the north'.

sources.title: Zhongshan (state)
sources.note: Wei conquest 407-406, independence regained 381, Lingshou capital 380-296, Zhao attacks from 307 and annexation in 296. Re-read 2026-10-19: Lingshou, Pingshan County, Dongyuan in Zhengding County, the Great Wall in Baoding and Tang County; Zhao 'surrounded Zhongshan almost entirely'.

sources.title: Wei (state)
sources.note: Wei identity: Anyi then Daliang, 403 to 225, rulers, 341 Maling, 225 flooding of Daliang; no area, no capital years. Re-read 2026-10-19: territory sentence ('parts of modern-day Henan, Hebei, Shanxi, and Shandong'), no Hedong, Henei or Ye, no dates for Anyi or Daliang.

sources.title: King Zhaoxiang of Qin
sources.note: Qin gains from Han, Wei, Zhao: Yiyang 307, Yique 293, Hedong 290, Anyi 286, Nanyang 273, Shangdang 262, Changping 260, Handan 259-257, Zhou 256.

sources.title: Zhang Yi (Warring States period)
sources.note: 328 campaign by which Qin acquired a large part of Wei.

sources.title: Eighteen Kingdoms
sources.note: Table of the Eighteen Kingdoms of 206 BCE with rulers and lands: Hán (Han Cheng), Western Wei (Wei Bao), Han (Liu Bang), the Three Qins, Zhao/Dai, Changshan, Yin, Henan.

sources.title: Chu-Han Contention
sources.note: 205-203 dated events: Henei, Wei Bao captured Oct-Nov 205, Chen Yu and Zhang Er, Zhang Er made King of Zhao 204, Xingyang 204, Hong Canal 203.

sources.title: Wei Bao
sources.note: Western Wei: capital Pingyang (Linfen), surrender to Liu Bang 205, Hedong Commandery absorbed it; Wei Bao died 204.

sources.title: Marquess Wen of Wei
sources.note: Wei conquests before 403: Wu Qi east of the Luo 409-406, Xihe Commandery, Zhongshan eliminated 406, 403 recognition.

sources.title: Kaifeng
sources.note: King Hui of Wei moved the capital from Anyi to Daliang in 361 BCE.

sources.title: Handan
sources.note: Who held Handan before 386: the page does not say (Jin from 588); 386 Marquess Jing of Zhao relocated the capital to Handan, Zhao's second capital after Zhongmu.

sources.title: Wey (state)
sources.note: Opened for the wey dossier's losses to Wei: 'By 320 BCE ... Wey controlled only the county of Puyang', 'Wey steadily declined due to internal strife and pressure from neighbors, especially Wei', 252 'making Wey a dependency of Wei'; 404 is not on the page.

sources.title: Battle of Huayang
sources.note: 275: Wei Ran besieges Daliang, Wei cedes eight unnamed cities and Wenyu (Wen County); 273: 'ceding the Nanyang region', not located on the page.

notes:
Wei (魏; Q320930). Q320930 is shared with Cliopatria's Cao Wei (220-265 CE): a different state, no relation. Western Wei (206-205, Wei Bao) and the 208-207 restored Wei are kept in this dossier as the same state revived (Cliopatria's Wei row runs to 204, as the Yan and Qi dossiers also keep their revivals). BIG PROBLEM in Cliopatria: every Warring States Wei shape from 404 to 223 lies on the Hebei plain (Hebei 342 of 429 cells in 404; 291 shape contains Datong, Baoding, Shijiazhuang, Dingzhou; no Henan cell). That is Zhongshan's and Zhao's land, and in Cliopatria the Zhao row sits on the Taihang and southern Shanxi. The dossier replaces it with discs at Anyi (Xia County, Shanxi), Xihe (Hancheng) and Daliang (Kaifeng); the radii are the researcher's reading of 'parts of modern Henan, Hebei, Shanxi and Shandong' (Wei page), so the replacement is rough. The Hebei plain from 381, when Zhongshan regained its independence (Zhongshan page), is left to the Zhongshan and Zhao dossiers. Pages opened: Wei (state), Zhongshan (state), Marquess Wen of Wei, Kaifeng, Zhang Yi (Warring States period), King Zhaoxiang of Qin, Qin's wars of unification, Eighteen Kingdoms, Chu-Han Contention, Wei Bao, Warring States period. The URL https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wei_(Warring_States) did not load (not found); Wei_(state) is the article. Not on any page: where Wei's boundary with Han, Zhao, Song, Qi ran; the Wei side of the 381 loss of Zhongshan (only the Zhongshan page dates it); the 273 cession of Nanyang by place; Wei Jiu's and Wei Bao's lands in 208-206 other than 'southern Shanxi'. The Qin dossier's 409/413 dates for Xihe differ from the Marquess Wen page (409-406). Gazetteer names wanted: Anyi (Xia County), Xihe, Hedong, Daliang already an alias of Kaifeng; coordinates used meanwhile.

Revision 2026-10-19 (after review ea-01-d). (1) Daliang disc 100 -> 60 km in every keyframe and the 225 loss: Xinzheng (72 km from Kaifeng) and Zheng's land are Han's from 375 (Han page: 'Han conquered and annexed Zheng'); the han dossier cuts the same disc from Zheng's land, so han and wei no longer overlap. (2) K0 (403-382): Cliopatria's whole Wei 404 shape (the Hebei plain with Handan, Xingtai, Ye) is cut to the Zhongshan core (Lingshou/Pingshan, Zhengding, Baoding), the only plain land the pages give Wei; the L1 loss of 381 and the found event use the same region. The disc set is the one the zhao dossier adds from 296; the future zhongshan dossier should use it. (3) After 381 the Hebei and Shandong parts of Wei (Wei page: 'parts of modern-day Henan, Hebei, Shanxi, and Shandong') and Henei are page-silent and left out (K1 note). (4) Western Wei's 206 gain: counterpart qin-dynasty, confidence 2. (5) 376 gain from Jin added (Warring States page). (6) Not mirrored, on purpose: the wey dossier's losses to Wei (L6 404 one cell, before Wei exists; L9 320, 27 cells round Puyang). The Wey page (opened 2026-10-19) names no taker ('pressure from neighbors, especially Wei'; 'a dependency of Wei' in 252), the cells lie 120 km from Daliang and 4 of them are in the shape the zhao dossier takes from Cliopatria (and Zhao gains 30 Wey cells in 247, zhao L19), so I read the counterpart 'wei' as the wey owner's guess and tell the wey owner: counterpart 'nobody' or leave unlocated. (7) The wars entry for the 273 'Nanyang' stays unlocated (Wei page does not mention Nanyang). Also noted: Cliopatria's 'Wei' 326-224 shapes contain Datong, Dai, Lingshou and Baoding (Zhao's northern land and Zhongshan) and its 'Zhao' 404 shape contains Linfen and Changzhi; I read the three Cliopatria rows as mislabelled against each other rather than as three accurate shapes, and use discs at the places the pages name. Addendum: the Battle of Huayang page gives the 275 cession of Wenyu (Wen County, Henei) and eight unnamed cities, and the 273 'Nanyang region' without a location (the wars entry for 273 stays as it is). Wenyu is held from 361 as a reading (Wei's Henei); the qin dossier has no matching 275 gain (qin owner: add Wenyu, Wei Ran's siege of Daliang). Wei Jiu's page did not load at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wei_Jiu (URL_NOT_FOUND); the 208 restoration year stays Cliopatria's.
